I could not get an exact fit. The three spin-allowed bands cannot all be matched with one (Dq, B) pair, so the values below are a least-squares compromise, and C is set by the spin-forbidden ¹E band.

**Method**

- For d⁸, the ³T₂g level sits at exactly 10Dq, so 7 400 cm⁻¹ gives Dq ≈ 740 cm⁻¹ on its own.
- The two ³T₁ levels (12 660 and 23 840 cm⁻¹) depend only on Dq and B; they do not depend on C.
- Minimising the residuals on ³T₂g, ³T₁(F) and ³T₁(P) together gives Dq ≈ 748 cm⁻¹ and B ≈ 934 cm⁻¹. At this point the predicted bands are 7 480, 12 602 and 23 848 cm⁻¹.
- The ¹E level depends on C (about 2 cm⁻¹ per unit of C). At Dq = 748 and B = 934 with C = 4 000, ¹E is predicted at 14 839 cm⁻¹, about 310 cm⁻¹ below the observed 15 150 cm⁻¹. Raising C by roughly 155 cm⁻¹ closes that gap, giving C ≈ 4 150 cm⁻¹.

The built-in fitting tool returned a poor fit (B ≈ 605 cm⁻¹, rms error ≈ 630 cm⁻¹) and mismatched the band assignments, so I did not use its result.

**Result (approximate)**

- Dq ≈ 748 cm⁻¹ (±20)
- B ≈ 934 cm⁻¹ (±20)
- C ≈ 4 150 cm⁻¹ (±100), giving C/B ≈ 4.4

The residuals are about 80 cm⁻¹ on ³T₂g and about 60 cm⁻¹ on the lower ³T₁ band. The ¹E band is the least reliable input because it is spin-forbidden, and its position is what sets C.
